title: RCW 19.28 — Electricians & Electrical Installations
description: Washington State law governing electrical contractor licensing, electrician certification, inspections, and enforcement. 30 questions.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.006, how is 'Basic electrical work Class A' defined?
choices: Electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding three stories and including not more than four dwelling units, or agricultural buildings
Electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding two stories and including not more than four dwelling units
Electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding three stories and including not more than two dwelling units
Electrical wiring of any residential structure regardless of stories or number of dwelling units
questions.answer: Electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding three stories and including not more than four dwelling units, or agricultural buildings
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006: 'Basic electrical work Class A' means electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding three stories in height and including not more than four dwelling units, or agricultural buildings.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.006, what distinguishes 'Basic electrical work Class B' from Class A?
choices: Class B covers structures with not more than one dwelling unit; Class A covers up to four dwelling units
Class B covers structures with not more than two dwelling units; Class A covers up to four dwelling units
Class B covers agricultural buildings only; Class A covers residential structures
Class B covers structures not exceeding two stories; Class A covers structures not exceeding three stories
questions.answer: Class B covers structures with not more than one dwelling unit; Class A covers up to four dwelling units
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006: 'Basic electrical work Class B' means electrical wiring of residential structures not exceeding three stories in height and including not more than one dwelling unit, whereas Class A allows up to four dwelling units.

questions.question: According to RCW 19.28.006, the term 'Administrator' refers to which of the following?
choices: A person who qualifies for a contractor's license by passing the required exams
The Director of the Department of Labor and Industries
A member of the Washington State electrical board
A person who supervises trainee electricians on a job site
questions.answer: A person who qualifies for a contractor's license by passing the required exams
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006: 'Administrator' means the person who qualifies for a contractor's license by passing the required examinations.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.006, which body is defined as the 'Board'?
choices: Washington State electrical board
Washington State Department of Labor and Industries
Washington State Building Code Council
The Governor's Office of Regulatory Compliance
questions.answer: Washington State electrical board
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006: 'Board' means the Washington State electrical board established under this chapter.

questions.question: How does RCW 19.28.006 define 'like-in-kind' replacement?
choices: Replacement of existing equipment with equipment of the same type and rating
Replacement of existing equipment with equipment of higher capacity and updated code compliance
Installation of any new equipment in place of removed outdated equipment
Repair of existing equipment without substitution of any components
questions.answer: Replacement of existing equipment with equipment of the same type and rating
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.006: 'Like-in-kind' means replacement of existing equipment with equipment of the same type and rating.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.041, how long does an electrical contractor license remain valid after issuance?
choices: 24 calendar months
12 calendar months
36 calendar months
18 calendar months
questions.answer: 24 calendar months
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.041: Electrical contractor licenses expire 24 calendar months after the date of issuance.

questions.question: What is the required bond amount for an electrical contractor license under RCW 19.28.041 and RCW 19.28.071?
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.041 and RCW 19.28.071: The required bond is $4,000 with the state of Washington as obligee, or a cash deposit of $4,000 as an alternative.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.041, which of the following is NOT listed as a required application element for an electrical contractor license?
choices: A copy of the applicant's journey level electrician certificate
UBI number
Workers' compensation account number
Excise tax registration number
questions.answer: A copy of the applicant's journey level electrician certificate
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.041: Required application elements include UBI number, workers' compensation account number, employment security account number, and excise tax registration number. A journey level certificate is not listed as a contractor license application requirement.

questions.question: According to RCW 19.28.041, who must be designated to qualify an electrical contractor license?
choices: A master electrician or administrator
A journey level electrician or specialty electrician
A state-licensed inspector or department employee
A board-approved safety officer
questions.answer: A master electrician or administrator
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.041: An electrical contractor license must designate a master electrician or administrator to qualify the license.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.091, a homeowner is exempt from electrical contractor licensing requirements when performing electrical work on their own single-family dwelling, provided the home is NOT offered for sale within how many months of the work?
choices: 12 months
6 months
24 months
18 months
questions.answer: 12 months
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.091: The owner of a single-family dwelling may perform their own electrical work without a contractor license, provided the work is not for hire and the property is not offered for sale within 12 months of the work being completed.

questions.question: Which of the following electrical installations is explicitly exempt from NEC requirements under RCW 19.28.010?
choices: Telephone wires under exclusive control of a communication utility
Panel boards in commercial buildings
Service entrance conductors in residential structures
Wiring in agricultural outbuildings
questions.answer: Telephone wires under exclusive control of a communication utility
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.010: Exemptions from NEC requirements include telephone, telegraph, radio, and TV (community antenna) wires that are under the exclusive control of communication utilities.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.021, if a dispute arises between a municipality and the state over electrical standards, arbitration is conducted by a panel of how many persons?
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.021: The arbitration panel consists of 5 persons — 2 appointed by the municipality, 2 appointed by the state, and 1 neutral member.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.021, a party wishing to appeal an arbitration decision regarding municipal vs. state electrical standards must file an appeal within how many days?
choices: 30 days
20 days
60 days
45 days
questions.answer: 30 days
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.021: An appeal of an arbitration decision must be filed with the superior court within 30 days of the decision.

questions.question: According to RCW 19.28.031, at whose expense does the Director obtain the current edition of the National Electrical Code (NEC) annually?
choices: State expense
Applicant's expense
Local jurisdiction's expense
The National Fire Protection Association's expense
questions.answer: State expense
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.031: The Director obtains the current edition of the NEC annually from the NFPA at state expense, and it is filed with the Director of Code Reviser.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.051, which THREE subject areas are covered by electrical examinations?
choices: Electrical safety, state electrical code, and electrical theory
Electrical safety, NEC code calculations, and business law
State electrical code, electrical theory, and labor law
Electrical theory, construction management, and electrical safety
questions.answer: Electrical safety, state electrical code, and electrical theory
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.051: The board establishes examinations covering three categories: (1) electrical safety, (2) state electrical code, and (3) electrical theory.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.201, how often must electrical certification examinations be offered at a minimum?
choices: At least twice per year
At least once per year
At least four times per year
At least once every six months, but only in odd-numbered years
questions.answer: At least twice per year
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.201: Certification examinations must be offered at least twice per year, and results are certified and sent to applicants.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.161, what is the maximum number of trainees a single certified journey level or specialty electrician may supervise?
choices: Two trainees
One trainee
Three trainees
Four trainees
questions.answer: Two trainees
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.161(2): A certified journey level electrician or specialty electrician may supervise not more than two trainees at one time (the 1:2 supervision ratio).

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.161, which certificate is required for an individual who is working toward electrician certification but has not yet passed the examination?
choices: Trainee certificate
Provisional specialty certificate
Apprentice contractor license
Temporary journey level permit
questions.answer: Trainee certificate
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.161: A trainee certificate is required for individuals who are working toward electrician certification and have not yet completed the examination process.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.101, which action is prohibited before an electrical installation has been inspected?
choices: Concealing the electrical installation
Energizing the installation for a load test
Applying for an occupancy permit
Connecting permanent fixtures to the panel
questions.answer: Concealing the electrical installation
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.101: It is prohibited to conceal electrical installations before they have been inspected by the Department.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.101, a utility shall NOT connect electrical service to a new installation until what condition is met?
choices: The installation has been approved or permitted
The contractor license has been renewed
A master electrician has certified the installation in writing
The local fire marshal has issued a clearance
questions.answer: The installation has been approved or permitted
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.101: A utility shall not connect service to an installation until the installation has been approved and/or permitted by the Department.

questions.question: According to RCW 19.28.241, which of the following is a valid ground for revoking an electrician's certificate of competency?
choices: Conviction of a felony related to the trade
Failure to complete a continuing education course in the current renewal period
Employing more than two trainees simultaneously
Working in a municipality without a local permit on one occasion
questions.answer: Conviction of a felony related to the trade
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.241: Grounds for revocation include fraud, gross incompetence, willful negligence, and conviction of a felony related to the electrical trade.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.341, a licensee wishing to appeal a license suspension or revocation must file an appeal within how many days?
choices: 20 days
30 days
10 days
45 days
questions.answer: 20 days
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.341: A licensee may appeal a license suspension or revocation to the board within 20 days, after which a board hearing is required.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.381, what action must the Department take if a licensee or certificate holder has outstanding unpaid penalties at the time of renewal?
choices: Deny renewal of the license or certificate
Issue a conditional renewal pending payment
Suspend the license for 30 days and then renew
Refer the matter to the Attorney General without taking action on renewal
questions.answer: Deny renewal of the license or certificate
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.381: The Department shall deny renewal if the licensee or certificate holder has outstanding unpaid penalties.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.351, where are all fees and penalties collected under RCW 19.28 deposited?
choices: The electrical license fund
The state general fund
The Department of Labor and Industries operating fund
The local jurisdiction's enforcement fund
questions.answer: The electrical license fund
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.351: All fees and penalties collected under this chapter are deposited into the electrical license fund, which is used to administer the electrical program.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.311, how many members make up the Washington State electrical board?
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.311: The Washington State electrical board consists of 7 members appointed by the Governor, serving staggered terms.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.321, which qualification must a state electrical inspector employed by the Department hold?
choices: Must be a qualified journey level electrician or master electrician
Must be a licensed electrical contractor with at least five years of experience
Must be a licensed professional engineer specializing in electrical systems
Must hold a specialty electrician certificate in at least two categories
questions.answer: Must be a qualified journey level electrician or master electrician
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.321: State electrical inspectors employed by the Department must be qualified journey level electricians or master electricians.

questions.question: Under the telecommunications subchapter (RCW 19.28.420), which of the following best describes the licensing requirement for telecommunications contractors?
choices: A separate telecommunications contractor license is required, distinct from the general electrical contractor license
A general electrical contractor license also covers all telecommunications work
Telecommunications work requires only a specialty electrician certificate, not a contractor license
No contractor license is required for low-voltage telecommunications systems
questions.answer: A separate telecommunications contractor license is required, distinct from the general electrical contractor license
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.420: A separate telecommunications contractor license is required for telecommunications work; it is not covered by a general electrical contractor license.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.400, which of the following systems is included in the definition of 'telecommunications systems'?
choices: Voice, data, audio/video, alarm, and fiber systems on the customer side of the network demarcation
High-voltage transmission lines and associated relay systems
Utility metering equipment and associated telemetry
Publicly owned street lighting and traffic signal systems
questions.answer: Voice, data, audio/video, alarm, and fiber systems on the customer side of the network demarcation
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.400 and RCW 19.28.410: Telecommunications systems include voice, data, audio/video, alarm, and fiber systems on the customer side of the network demarcation point.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.501, what financial assurance requirement applies specifically to telecommunications contractors that differs from electrical contractors?
choices: Telecommunications contractors must carry liability insurance, in addition to or instead of only a bond
Telecommunications contractors must post a $10,000 bond instead of the $4,000 bond required of electrical contractors
Telecommunications contractors must deposit $8,000 cash with the Department
Telecommunications contractors are exempt from all bond and insurance requirements
questions.answer: Telecommunications contractors must carry liability insurance, in addition to or instead of only a bond
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.501: Telecommunications contractors are required to carry liability insurance, which is a requirement distinct from the bond-only requirement applicable to general electrical contractors.

questions.question: Under RCW 19.28.095, what type of electrical work is covered by the equipment repair specialty classification?
choices: Repair or replacement of existing electrical equipment with like-in-kind replacements
New installation of electrical equipment in previously unequipped areas
Upgrade of existing electrical equipment to higher-rated components
Installation of temporary power supplies for construction sites
questions.answer: Repair or replacement of existing electrical equipment with like-in-kind replacements
questions.explanation: RCW 19.28.095: The equipment repair specialty covers repair or replacement of existing electrical equipment with like-in-kind replacements and does not cover new installation.
